- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `90f3dc81862768560f24859ba933c961bf2590da` — the merge of head `33d98946db09522a9bf66a67f64e53e98716efdc` into base `ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 90f3dc81862768560f24859ba933c961bf2590da && git checkout 90f3dc81862768560f24859ba933c961bf2590da
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd 33d98946db09522a9bf66a67f64e53e98716efdc && git checkout -B drift-repro ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd && git merge --no-ff 33d98946db09522a9bf66a67f64e53e98716efdc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ec44cf60bf44cb7505a9e674cda22e3a398025bd` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

The PR widens the accept set in two places and the public surface in one. Each change the two hunks imply, judged:

1. **`PageComponentType` gains `'record:json'`** (page.zod.ts:212) — **right.** The reserved `record` namespace, so `hasReservedComponentNamespace` holds; `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES` and `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPE_CANDIDATES` derive from the enum and the map (component-type-vocabulary.ts:95-115), so `component-type-unknown` offers `'record:json'` for a near spelling with no table edit (pinned in validate-record-json-23745.test.ts with a `record:jsn` probe). A new block rather than a widened one follows the ruling's own test (objectui#12438 letter C, item 2) and the card's fit-check measurements: no declared block draws a record value as JSON, and `record:details` draws JSON only for a declared `json` field.

2. **`ComponentPropsMap['record:json'] = RecordJsonProps`** (component.zod.ts:8313), a `strictObject` row — **right.** A node naming the type now has its `properties` judged rather than skipped. Two derived consumers widen with it and need no edit: `RECORD_CONTEXT_BLOCK_TAGS` is built from the map by the `record:` prefix (react-blocks.ts:188-192), so a react page writing the `RecordJson` tag is refused by `react-block-needs-record-context` the day this lands; `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES` is pinned only for the four withdrawn blocks (react-blocks.test.ts:117-124), so no entry is owed. `check-yaml-examples.ts` dispatches any corpus node against the row; none exists yet. The map-vs-enum parity pins (component-type-vocabulary.test.ts:44-51) hold on both sides.

3. **`RecordJsonProps` is a new public export, const and type** (api-surface +2, declaration-map, export-origins, json-schema.manifest, authorable-surface +3 keys) — **right.** `type RecordJsonProps = z.input` with the ADR-0122 isomorphic pin (787 to 788 in type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts): the shape carries no default and no transform (a `regex` string, a lazy `I18nLabelSchema` union, a string array), so `z.input` equals `z.infer` and no `Parsed` alias is owed. `Type Check · source gates` is green on the head, which is the tsc proof of the pin.

4. **`field`: required, grammar `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`** — **right.** The same inline grammar the house uses for object and field names (data/field.zod.ts:1143, component.zod.ts:1125 `SECTION_COUNT_FIELD_PATTERN`; identifiers.zod.ts:44-46 records the inline restatement as the convention, not a constant to import). It is deliberately absent from `COMPONENT_FIELD_SPECS` (validate-page-field-bindings.ts:205); judged in ③ Q1.

5. **`label`: `I18nLabelSchema.optional()`** — **right.** Ten sibling rows in the same file declare `label` the same way, and `COMPONENT_NODE_KEYS_GUIDANCE` excludes `label` from the node-only set precisely because it is a declared prop almost everywhere in this file, so the row and the guidance set it carries do not contradict each other.

6. **`requiredPermissions`: `z.array(z.string().min(1)).min(1)`, REQUIRED, fail-CLOSED by its describe** — **right.** It is a separate declaration from the shared fail-open `RECORD_BLOCK_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS_DESCRIPTION` (component.zod.ts:1091), which the diff leaves untouched at all four sites (:1579, :1779, :1884, :2329); the "one key, one text" pin (component-record-block-field-security.test.ts:239-255) still compares only those four against `RecordQuickActionsProps`, and the census pin was widened to name `record:json` beside them (:195-199). The element `.min(1)` is one notch tighter than the card's proposal: a narrowing applied to a surface that has never been published is not a narrowing of anything shipped, and on the card's own fail-closed reasoning a gate naming an empty capability is one nobody passes. Under ADR-0049 the key is a security-named property whose describe states it is presentation only and authorises nothing, the same posture and the same `[ADR-0066]` tag the four shipped blocks carry; the renderer that honours it is owed by objectui#12490 step 4, which the card chain blocks until this spec is installable. That is the `record:approval_decision` route (commit `7731d7018`: the same six-file shape, declared spec first), not a quiet reversal of a recorded decision.

7. **`PRINT_REFUSED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` gains `record:json`** (page.zod.ts:1382) — **right, and required**: page-print.test.ts:185-190 refuses an unclassified live member, and the reason is worded to the pin's grammar (lowercase start, no full stop, :216-219). A collapsed panel behind a per-viewer gate is correctly refused rather than printed.

8. **Aliases `key`/`path`/`fieldName` to `field`, `title`/`summary` to `label`, `permissions`/`requiredCapabilities` to `requiredPermissions`** — **right.** Every target is a declared key and no alias is itself declared, which is the `aliases` contract in strict-object.ts:137-151; the `alias-integrity` audit that rejects a dead entry sits in the green `Lint` family.

9. **Not widened, correctly:** `COMPONENT_FIELD_SPECS` (deliberate, ③ Q1); `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES` (optional per block); the liveness ledger (③ flag 2); the strictness ledger moves 213 to 214 sites and 202 to 203 strict for the one new `strictObject` call site, which is the count the diff implies.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23745-record-json-block.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, body carries `Clause-②: yes` with no arm; the PR body carries the same line. It removes, renames or tightens nothing that was shipped, so no migration and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md §3) and `minor` is the right level for an additive widening of a released package; `skip-changeset` does not apply and is not claimed. 1. `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` outside the claim's file surface — **answered, accepted.** `check:spec-parsed-alias` (ADR-0122) reds on a new exported schema without a `Parsed` name or an iso pin; the pin is the ADR's prescribed route for a transform-free shape, and the PR body names it.
2. No liveness row — **answered, accepted.** `page.json` classifies `regions` as a live, undrilled container (#4956) and its component read-point list is evidence-only; `record:json` has no renderer or producer to cite, so a row would be invented evidence. The precedent commit for `record:approval_decision` touched no liveness file, and `Spec property liveness` is green on this head. The read point to cite will exist at objectui#12490 step 4.
3. `.min(1)` elements and the alias table — **answered, accepted** (① items 6 and 8).
4. One single-file vitest run outside the verify lock — **answered**: a process note with no bearing on the contract; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts.
5. Commit trailer form — **answered**: a process note, not a contract matter.

Open questions (two):

- **Q1 — `field` is not judged against declared fields.** Options A keep as shipped / B widen `attachedOnRead` / C new list or rule; the dev recommends A. **Answered: A for this head.** The key this block exists for (`payload` on `sys_approval_request`) is served by the read route beside the declared fields, so an entry in `COMPONENT_FIELD_SPECS` would refuse the one page that will author it (#23746); the lint pin proves the asymmetry with a firing `record:highlights` control. B widens a ruled declaration (`attachedOnRead`, #22211 ruling A) whose leaves are a fixed scalar set, for one speculative key; C is a gate nobody ordered. The silent-miss boundary is stated in the describe, the schema header and the changeset, which keeps the claim as narrow as the enforcement (Prime Directive #10). **Escalated to the dispatching seat, not a blocker:** a misspelled `field` that draws nothing with no publish-time refusal is an authoring trap by Prime Directive #10's own definition, so it should carry a card, not only a describe. File the B follow-up (judge `record:json.field` against fields plus a served-key declaration) as a p3 card chained after #23746, so the trap has an owner when a second served-key consumer appears.
- **Q2 — `label` as `I18nLabelSchema` versus a plain string.** **Answered: A, as shipped.** The declaration matches the ten sibling `label` rows in the same file, and with no renderer yet the spec is the contract the renderer is built to. **Carried to the dispatching seat:** objectui#12490 step 4's dispatch should name the `pickLocalized` pin on the summary line explicitly, so the locale map is declared-and-read rather than declared-and-ignored.

- PR #23708 (open, a breaking `feat(spec)!` on other regions of page.zod.ts) is the lane's normal-concurrency rule per the claim: whichever lands second merges `main`. Per the claim's reading it does not touch `PageComponentType` or the print pair; not re-read here. A textual overlap surfaces in the queue; it is not a contract matter at this head.
